component.name: BlinkTable
component.summary: Compare, measure and prove image quality — pick the keeper

description.p: BlinkTable is a workspace where image and video quality is compared, measured and proven: split, zoom, magnifiers, difference modes, objective metrics, a ranked verdict and an export that matches what is on screen. It is built for photographers, retouchers, upscaling and ML pipelines, and anyone who has to compare images at pixel level without losing context.
Three workspaces over one rendering path:

ul.li: Image Compare: two images under a movable horizontal or vertical split, with zoom, pan and one or more synchronized magnifiers that each carry their own capture area, size, freeze mode, color and keyboard position.
Multi Compare: a grid for any number of images that grows as needed, with synchronized zoom and pan, a dimmed focused slot and the same magnifier vocabulary.

Image Gallery: open a folder and get series with 0-100 quality scores, Grid and List views, sorting by Rank, Name, Date or AI quality, and triage that keeps your selection — Keep best, Reject, Remove from view, Clean rejected with Undo, Compare finalists.
Algorithms ranks a series by measured quality; opt-in AI ranking reads the same metrics with a model, and a hand-picked winner is shown as Ranked by Manual.
Ask AI works on a card, a selection or a series. Answers are advisory and carry the AI read, unverified badge; the key is stored unencrypted and saved metrics can be reset at any time.
Difference and channel modes, guide lines, filename overlays and a magnifier that maps to the crop box keep the judgment on the actual pixels.
Record a comparison session and edit it in the built-in video editor — timeline selection, trimming, preview playback and export; a disk thumbnail cache keeps the strip responsive.
Export the full-resolution comparison with overlays, labels and the comparison state preserved, so the exported file matches what was on screen.

An MCP server ships with the app: a local stdio server with 23 tools for UI inventory, actions, state, logs, traces, screenshots, keystrokes and jobs, so an agent can drive and inspect a running instance.
Keyboard navigation reaches the whole app — tabs, dialogs, lists, the canvas, the video editor and the sliders; arrows navigate, Enter edits a value, Esc reverts, and shortcuts are remappable.
Contextual F1 help, illustrated topics and Learn more from every action in Find Action; a global Interface Scale resizes the entire UI from 0.5 to 2.5.

description.p: 11.0.1 removes the "untested export size" warning from every export path, so saving a comparison no longer stops at a dialog no user action could satisfy. The visible identity is BlinkTable everywhere it appears, and the store listing carries new screenshots.

11.0.0 adds Image Gallery with AI-assisted triage, a local MCP server for agents, and a global Interface Scale; keyboard navigation now reaches the rest of the app, and the canvas, Multi Compare, the video editor and help all get a substantial update.

ul.li: Image Gallery: a new tab — open a folder, get series, 0-100 quality scores, Grid and List views, sorting by Rank, Name, Date or AI quality, and a filter that keeps your selection.

AI ranking: one reading per metric, Algorithms ranking by measured quality, opt-in AI (Jev) ranking, a hand-picked winner shown as Ranked by Manual, and Ask AI on a card, a selection or a series — answers are advisory and carry the AI read, unverified badge.
Triage: Keep best, Reject, Remove from view (files stay on disk), Clean rejected to _rejected/ with Undo, Compare finalists (up to 12) and Reset metrics cache.
MCP server: a local stdio server with 23 tools (11 read-only, 12 that change state) for UI inventory, actions, state, logs, traces, screenshots, simulated keystrokes, jobs and wait_for.
Keyboard: Quick Look filmstrip, editable sliders, and keyboard-reachable dialogs, session picker, list pickers, tab strip and video editor, with focus rings for keyboard input.
Canvas and Multi Compare: clean rendering of large images, a magnifier that maps to the crop box, stable overlays, and a grid that grows past the old 12-slot cap.
Video editor: a disk thumbnail cache keeps the strip responsive and the export tabs are keyboard-reachable.
Help and appearance: contextual F1 topics, illustrated pages, Learn more from Find Action, and a global Interface Scale (0.5-2.5) that applies immediately.
Upgrading: sli-ui-toolkit 4.2.4 is required; torch, piq and pyvips are new hard dependencies; AI is opt-in and MCP clients should re-run tools/list.

description.p: Fix multiple inheritance crashes in UI and update to sli-ui-toolkit 3.1.9
A major release focused on smoother canvas interaction, sharper rendering, and a richer multi-magnifier workflow.

ul.li: Smoother zoom and panning in the main comparison canvas, with more responsive feedback during interactive movement.
Cleaner image rendering with corrected alpha handling, so anti-aliased edges, magnifier circles, and overlays look crisp both on screen and in screenshots.
Reworked multi-magnifier workflow: easier to add, hide, delete, and manage multiple magnifiers, each with its own color and settings.
Optional automatic color assignment for new magnifiers and optional intersection highlighting while dragging capture areas.
More consistent behavior across comparison modes, guide lines, capture rings, filename overlays, and exported images.
Smoother live interactions: separators, splits, and magnifier dividers move without lag and stay in sync with the cursor.
Better compatibility with Flatpak: removed the direct DBus notification path that caused integration issues.
Updated in-app help to cover the expanded magnifier behavior and new canvas controls.

description.p: A major release consolidating months of deep architectural work and introducing significant new features.

ul.li: Hybrid CPU-GPU rendering: a new rendering engine capable of offloading work to the GPU via OpenGL shaders for dramatically improved performance on large images.
Canvas architecture overhaul: the comparison canvas was fully rewritten for correctness and performance across all operating modes and edge cases.
Native Qt widgets: all pop-up and overlay windows are now native Qt widgets, greatly improving Wayland compatibility.
Canvas zooming and panning: the main comparison view can now be zoomed and panned interactively.
Video editor improvements: the timeline was rewritten with keyframe-based model, aspect-ratio-correct thumbnails, and dynamic spacing.
Plugin-based architecture for extensibility and a cleaner internal structure.

description.p: This release includes various improvements and bug fixes.

This is the most extensive architectural refactoring in the project's history, transitioning the entire application to a robust and modern Model-View-Presenter (MVP) pattern. This update establishes a new, stable foundation for future development and introduces a completely custom-built UI.

ul.li: Complete Architectural Overhaul: The codebase is now fully modular and based on the MVP pattern, significantly improving stability and maintainability. Many underlying bugs have been passively fixed as a result.

New Custom UI: The third-party `PyQt-Fluent-Widgets` library has been removed and replaced with a custom-built set of "fluent-style" components. This removes GPL licensing constraints and gives the application a more unique design.
Enhanced Image List Management: The image selection flyout is now a powerful two-panel manager with full drag-and-drop support for reordering and moving images between lists.
New and Reimagined Dialogs: Introduced a dedicated, feature-rich Export dialog and a redesigned, easier-to-navigate Help window.
Improved Caching: The caching system has been upgraded from two to three levels for even smoother performance during interactive use.
Reduced Package Size: The removal of the external UI library has decreased the application's overall size on some platforms.

description.p: This is a major quality-of-life and rendering engine update.

ul.li: Overhauled the core update logic to a reactive, state-driven architecture, significantly improving stability and eliminating a class of race-condition bugs.
The magnifier can now render outside the image boundaries and correctly handles horizontal split view.
Added smooth, anti-aliased borders for the magnifier and capture area for better visual quality.
Added long-press actions for swapping and clearing images/lists to speed up workflow.
Image selection dropdowns are now scrollable with the mouse wheel.
Added a new setting to permanently enable or disable debug logging.
Replaced all internal print statements with a structured logging system.

description.p: This release introduces a major user interface overhaul and performance improvements.

ul.li: The application interface has been completely redesigned using the modern `qfluentwidgets` style.
The image caching service has been significantly improved, resulting in a much smoother experience.
Refactored the core rendering code for better performance and easier maintenance.

description.p: This release focuses on settings persistence and bug fixes.

ul.li: Added window state persistence: the app now remembers its size and position between sessions.
Introduced a new Settings dialog to centralize application preferences.
Added options to configure UI language, JPEG save quality, and the maximum length of displayed filenames.
Addressed several critical bugs to improve stability.
